The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 09.08.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 09.08.2021, at about 1.30 a.m. when he was proceeding in the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-06-D-8769 after loading the tomatoes grown in the land of one Nagesh to sell the same at Kolar Market and when they reached near Kottanuru Gate,
NH-7 Road, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura District, at that time the driver of the Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK-06-CB-5179 which was moving ahead of the petitioner's vehicle suddenly turned his vehicle from right side towards left side in a rash and negligent manner, caused the accident, due to which front portion of the Eicher vehicle completely damaged and the petitioner sustained injuries.

It is stated that he has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.

It is further stated that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as collie Ramanjaneya Alias Ramanji vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28425199/
2 and doing agriculture and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK-06-CB- 5179.

Hence,
the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending Tata Truck are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has entered its appearance through its learned counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.
5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards the medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further denied the alleged negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.
UK-06-CB-5179 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and also the valid and effective driving licence held by the drive of the offending vehicle, valid permit and FC.
Owner of the vehicle and the jurisdictional police have not complied section 134(C)and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has also contented that there is delay in lodging the complaint before the police.
It is the contention of the respondent No.1 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 09.08.2021 at about 1.30 a.m., near Kottanuru Gate, NH-7 Road, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura district, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK- 06-CB-5179?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked 20 documents as per Ex.P1 to 20.

On the other hand,
respondent No.1 has not led defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. Issues No.1: As per the case of the petitioner, on 09.08.2021, at about 1.30 a.m. when he was proceeding in the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-06-D-8769 after loading the tomatoes grown in the land of one Nagesh to sell the same at Kolar Market and when they reached near Kottanuru Gate,
NH-7 Road, Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura District, at that time the driver of the said Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK-06-CB-5179 which was moving ahead of the petitioner's vehicle suddenly turned his vehicle from right side to left side in a rash and negligent manner, caused the accident,
due to which front portion of the Eicher vehicle completely damaged and the petitioner sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, Seizure mahazar, Sketch, IMV report, 133 noitce and reply, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 10.
11.

According to the version of petitioner, the accident happened near Kottanuru Gate, NH-7 Road,
Nandi Hobli, Chikkaballapura District, when the driver of Tata Truck bearing Reg.
No.UK-06-CB-5179, which was moving ahead of the petitioner's vehicle suddenly turned his vehicle from right side to left side with out any indication at about 1.30 a.m in a negligent manner, due to which front portion of the petitioner's Eicher vehicle completely damaged and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P5 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.
On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P5

it reflects that injured was traveling in the Eicher canter as a inmate, the driver of the Tata Truck came in a negligent manner with out observing the up coming the vehicle suddenly taken his vehicle towards right side to left side and dashed against the petitioner's vehicles.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.

If the driver of the Truck had taken proper care and precaution regarding the vehicles which are plying on the main road,
then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P.6 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P10 was also filed as against the driver of the Tata Truck.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 5 and 6 coupled with Ex.P.10 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving by the Tata Truck driver.
12. Even in the instant case the driver of the Tata Truck is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tata Truck bearing registration No. UK-06-CB-5179 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK-06-CB-5179.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tata Truck bearing Reg. No.UK-06-CB-5179.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as coolie and agriculture and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but there is not any document towards proof of income.
Hence, in the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2021.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.3.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained comminuted fracture of the left proximal tibia with fibula fracture and right bimalleloar fracture and the petitioner has undergone surgery of ORIF with plate and screw and got discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

On examination, the petitioner is complains of pain and weakness in the left knee, unable to sit down and sit cross legged and it is found that the petitioner has swollen left knee restricted left knee movements.

He assessed 40%
disability to the left lower limb and 13% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.3 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 36 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 09.08.2021.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P16 Adhaar card as 01.01.1985, the petitioner was aged 36 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 36 is 15 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text: PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The wound certificate marked at Ex.P9 discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Further the Ex.P11 Discharge Summary of Rajarajeshwari Medical College Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 09.08.2021 to 27.08.2021 and underwent ORIF with plate and screw.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.42,621/- as per Ex.P13.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.42,621/- and he is entitled for the same.
17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 18 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/- (15,000X4) under this head.
19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 36 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 12% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.25,000/- on this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.

Thus he is entitled to Ramanjaneya Alias Ramanji vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28425199/
6 Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.
21.

Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount  No. Compensation  1. Loss of future earnings due Rs. 3,24,000/-
 to disability  2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 42,621/-
 4. Conveyance, food and Rs. 20,000/-
 nourishment, attendant  charges and other incidental  expenses.
 5. Loss of income during laid Rs.
 up period 60,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 25,000/-
 comforts and expectancy of  life  7.
Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,51,621/-.
22. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Truck bearing Reg.
No.UK-06-CB-5179.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
It is not disputed that 1 st respondent is the insurer and 2nd respondent is the owner.
Hence, 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,51,621/-(Rupees five lakhs fifty one thousand six hundred and twenty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.5,21,621/-(excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 60% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
